goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — Credential-sync requests omit the configured secret header, so an externally authenticated sync endpoint cannot verify these callers.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, the code makes a fetch request to the sync endpoint but does NOT include the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header. Compare this to apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-26 which expects and validates the webhook secret header (CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME). The refreshOAuthTokens function only sends calcomUserId and appSlug in the body, missing the authentication header that the receiving endpoint requires. This is a security/correctness bug where the credential sync requests will fail authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61 — Concurrent first-time sync requests can both miss findFirst and create duplicate credentials.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in the new webhook handler. Looking at lines 57-77 in app-credential.ts, the code does a findFirst to check if a credential exists, then either updates or creates based on the result. If two concurrent requests arrive for the same userId/appId combination, both could execute findFirst before either creates, causing both to miss the existing record and attempt to create duplicates. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition. The code should use upsert or a transaction with proper locking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The helper unifies HTTP responses and provider SDK results behind `any`, leaving integrations coupled to an undocumented return shape.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens returns `any` type (line 3: `async (refreshFunction: () => any, appSlug: string, userId: number | null)`). The function can return either a fetch Response object (from the credential sync endpoint) or whatever the refreshFunction returns (which varies by integration - could be SDK objects, fetch responses, etc.). This creates an undocumented contract where callers must handle different return shapes. This is a legitimate architectural concern about type safety and API design introduced by this new helper function, though not a bug since the code may work at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Accepting `any` and `ZodTypeAny` erases each provider's token contract before credential persistence.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that parseRefreshTokenResponse accepts `any` for the response and `z.ZodTypeAny` for the schema (lines 12-13 in the new file). This is a design concern - the function uses a generic schema parameter but the return type loses the specific token structure. Looking at the diff, the function is used in multiple places (GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, ZoomVideoApiAdapter, SalesforceCalendarService) where previously type-specific schemas were used directly. The function does parse with the provided schema, but the `any` input type and generic return could allow type mismatches. This is a legitimate architectural concern about type safety in the new abstraction, though not a bug since the runtime behavior should be correct if schemas are passed correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5 — This duplicates the request-state parsing in `decodeOAuthState` only to serialize it again, creating two parsers to maintain.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for encodeOAuthState.ts, it only shows a simple file rename/move with an import path change. The file content shows it parses req.query.state and returns a base64 encoded string. The finding claims it 'duplicates the request-state parsing in decodeOAuthState only to serialize it again', but encodeOAuthState and decodeOAuthState serve opposite purposes - one encodes state for OAuth flow initiation, the other decodes it on callback. They are not duplicating each other; they are complementary functions. The diff only shows import path changes, not any actual code duplication being introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The sync path casts a fetch Response to HubspotToken, persisting/using undefined token fields instead of the endpoint payload.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call in refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of refreshFunction() (the hubspot SDK call). When the sync path is taken, it returns a raw fetch Response, but the code at line 177+ treats the return value as HubspotToken directly (hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken). This is a type mismatch - a fetch Response is not a HubspotToken, so accessing token fields would be undefined. This is a real bug in the credential sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no deadline, so an unavailable sync endpoint can indefinitely block OAuth refreshes on request paths.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, the fetch call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/deadline configured. If the sync endpoint is slow or unavailable, this fetch will hang indefinitely, blocking the OAuth refresh flow. This is a real defect - network calls should have timeouts to prevent indefinite blocking. The diff clearly shows a bare fetch() with no AbortController or timeout mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset webhook secret makes an absent request header compare equal and permits unauthenticated credential writes.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the code checks: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then undefined !== undefined is false, so the check passes. This allows unauthenticated access when the webhook secret is not configured. The APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED check at line 17-19 does require CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET to be set (as seen in constants.ts), but this is a truthy check - an empty string would fail that check but still allow the security bypass. More importantly, if someone sets only CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY but not CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, the feature would be enabled but the auth check would be bypassable.
